In November 2025, the White House launched the Genesis Mission, a plan to transform US federal research through AI. A few weeks earlier, Brussels had published its strategy for AI in science; London followed with its own. In July 2026, Beijing presented a plan for autonomous laboratories. Behind these strategies lies a shift in power: the most advanced instruments of discovery now belong to a handful of private companies, which set their prices, their conditions of access and sometimes their agenda. This article compares the public strategies and describes how much weight France and Europe can really carry.
Pendant des décennies, les grands instru: For decades, the major instruments of science (accelerators, telescopes, supercomputers) were public or international. The most capable AI models are private, mostly American, and subject to Washington’s export controls. How are states taking back control? Are universities becoming customers or partners? And can Europe build a capability of its own without isolating itself?

Le décret présidentiel du 24 novembre 20: The executive order of 24 November 2025 tasks the Department of Energy with creating a “closed-loop experimentation platform” integrating supercomputers and federal data, in order to produce scientific foundation models and run robotic laboratories. Priority fields: biotechnology, critical materials, fission and fusion, space, quantum information, semiconductors. Goal: to sharply increase the productivity of federal R&D “within a decade” (White House).
Le 18 décembre 2025, le DOE annonçait de: On 18 December 2025, the DOE announced memoranda of understanding with 24 organisations, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, AMD, AWS, xAI, Periodic Labs and Radical AI (DOE). These are statements of intent to collaborate, with no scientific results at this stage. Microsoft then committed $60 million ($40 million in Azure credits, $20 million in services) (Microsoft).
Le modèle américain est un partenariat p: The American model is a public-private partnership in which the state provides data, national laboratories and legitimacy, and companies provide models and cloud. It comes with political control over access: the suspension of Fable 5 and Mythos 5 in June 2026 under export controls (MobiHealthNews) and the restriction of Mythos 5.1 to US organisations (Anthropic) are its concrete expression.
Chine : l&#39;« AI for Science » municip: China: municipal and national “AI for Science”
Selon le média d&#39;État ECNS, repris p: According to the state media outlet ECNS, as reported by Let's Data Science, Beijing published a plan in early July 2026 to become a global hub for AI-assisted research by 2028: autonomous laboratories combining AI, robotics and high-throughput instruments, a general-purpose scientific AI platform, research vouchers. Fields: physics, materials, health, life sciences, quantum, biological breeding. There is a single source and the budgets are not known: the information is unconfirmed in its details. On the model side, Chinese open models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM) are among the comparison benchmarks cited by Mistral (Mistral AI): China’s weight comes above all from open weights.
Royaume-Uni : la mission chiffrée: United Kingdom: a mission with numbers attached
La stratégie AI for Science du 20 novemb: The AI for Science strategy of 20 November 2025 devotes up to £137 million, drawn from an AI budget of £2 billion for 2026–2030, to three pillars: data (data from UKRI facilities compliant with the FAIR principles by 2030), compute (access to the AI Research Resource, including Isambard-AI, from 10,000 to 1.4 million GPU hours), skills (at least 1,000 researchers trained). First mission: trial-ready medicines in 100 days by 2030 (techUK).
Union européenne : RAISE et les gigafact: European Union: RAISE and the gigafactories
La stratégie européenne pour l&#39;IA da: The European strategy for AI in science (8 October 2025) rests on RAISE, a “virtual institute” pooling compute, data, talent and funding, and provides €600 million from Horizon Europe for researchers’ access to compute, notably to the gigafactories, as well as a doubling of Horizon Europe’s annual investment in AI to more than €3 billion (European Commission). The RAISE pilot, launched in November 2025, has €33 million (2025 programme) followed by €107 million (2026–2027), with calls on laboratory automation in materials science planned for 2027 (European Commission). The call to select up to seven gigafactories is open until 3 December 2026 (EuroHPC).

Les montants publics européens et britan: European and British public amounts are small compared with the more than $400 billion invested by five large technology companies in 2025 (IEA). The comparison is not direct (infrastructure investment versus research budgets), but it indicates the order of magnitude.

Les entreprises ne vendent plus seulemen: Companies no longer just sell tools; they organise researchers’ access:
OpenAI offre un accès gratuit à 100 000: OpenAI offers free access to 100,000 researchers until 2027 and claims more than $250 million committed to external research; among the first institutions: the IAS and the ENS (OpenAI).
Anthropic ouvre 10 000 places gratuites: Anthropic is opening 10,000 free or discounted places for academic laboratories and up to $50,000 in credits per project (Anthropic).
Google ouvre Co-Scientist aux chercheurs: Google is opening Co-Scientist to researchers via Gemini for Science (Google DeepMind).
Ces programmes réduisent les inégalités: These programmes reduce inequalities of access in the short term, but they create habits, dependencies and data flows towards the providers. The Leiden Declaration calls on governments to “regulate the AI industry and invest in public alternatives”, and on industrial collaborations to meet the same standards as academic research (Leiden University).
Les universités gardent la fonction de v: Universities retain the validation function: peer review, replication, training. They are even becoming its bottleneck: mathematicians refuse to validate announcements that come without a paper (Article 5), and arXiv is rationing submissions. On the other hand, they are losing control of the instruments.
Côté industrie, les stratégies divergent: On the industry side, strategies diverge: Eli Lilly is building its own AI factory of 1,016 GPUs and opening its models to other biotechs through federated learning (NVIDIA); Isomorphic Labs is multiplying collaborations with large pharmaceutical companies (Isomorphic Labs); start-ups such as Periodic Labs are building private autonomous laboratories (Periodic Labs). Philanthropic organisations (HHMI Janelia, Arc Institute, FutureHouse) occupy an intermediate space, often a more open one.
Les grandes puissances ont toutes adopté: The major powers all adopted an explicit strategy for AI in science between 2025 and 2026 (official documents).
L&#39;accès aux modèles les plus capable: Access to the most capable models has become an instrument of US foreign policy (documented fact).
L&#39;Europe dispose d&#39;une infrastru: Europe has world-class public computing infrastructure (documented fact).
L&#39;efficacité de ces stratégies : auc: The effectiveness of these strategies: none has yet produced a measurable result at national scale.

<span class=\"n\">09</span>Enjeux économ: 09Economic, industrial, public and geopolitical stakes for France
La France a des atouts rares : un acteur: France has rare assets: a player capable of training a large model (Mistral, €3 billion raised in September 2026, according to TechCrunch); Jean Zay and soon Alice Recoque; research organisations (CNRS, CEA, Inserm, Inria) that run programmes such as the PEPR DIADEM on materials (CNRS); health data among the most comprehensive in the world, now hosted by a French provider (Le Monde).
Ses faiblesses sont connues : budgets pu: Its weaknesses are well known: modest public budgets, dependence on American chips, fragmented initiatives, and prestigious institutions (the ENS) adopting American tools on an individual basis. Three levers seem within reach:
Une négociation européenne collective de: A collective European negotiation of access to frontier models, with guarantees of continuity.
Un investissement ciblé dans les données: Targeted investment in high-quality scientific data (including negative results) from major research facilities, which foreign models cannot produce on their own.
Le soutien aux modèles ouverts spécialis: Support for specialised open models, where the gap with the giants is small and reproducibility is high.
Protocoles d&#39;accord et intentions, p: Memoranda of understanding and intentions, not results
Un plan municipal rapporté par une sourc: A municipal plan reported by a single source
Contribution d&#39;Horizon Europe à l&#3: Horizon Europe’s contribution to access to compute, notably to the gigafactories
Programme limité, sur candidature ou tir: A limited programme, by application or lottery, for a fixed period
Peut désigner la localisation, le droit: Can refer to location, applicable law, ownership of the model or ownership of the chips
Crédits et licences, souvent dans ses pr: Credits and licences, often for its own tools
La géopolitique de l&#39;IA pour la scie: The geopolitics of AI for science pits models of organisation against each other more than countries: a public-private partnership under state control in the United States, planning and open models in China, targeted missions in the United Kingdom, pooling and regulation in Europe. No strategy has yet proved itself. For Europe, the risk is not missing out on the race for models, which has already largely been run, but becoming a captive customer of instruments it does not control, while supplying the data and validations that give them their value.
